title: Greeting to the Roman Church
english: Ignatius, who is also called God-Bearer, to the church that has found mercy in the majesty of the Most High Father and of Jesus Christ, his only Son: to the church beloved and enlightened by the will of the One who willed all things that are, in keeping with the love of Jesus Christ our God; to the church that presides in the land of the Romans, worthy of God, worthy of honor, worthy of blessing, worthy of praise, worthy of success, worthy of purity, presiding over love, bearing the name of Christ and the name of the Father. Her I greet in the name of Jesus Christ, the Son of the Father.

To all who are one in flesh and spirit with every commandment of his, who are filled with the grace of God without wavering and freed from every foreign taint: heartiest greetings, blameless, in Jesus Christ our God.
orientation: Ignatius opens his letter to the church in Rome, praising it with a chain of honorific titles and greeting its members in the name of Jesus Christ.

title: Ignatius fears the Romans' love may hinder his martyrdom
english: I prayed to God, and I have succeeded in seeing your faces, which are worthy of God. I was asking for even more than this. For I am bound in Christ Jesus, and I hope to greet you, if it is God's will that I be deemed worthy to reach the end.

The beginning is well ordered, if indeed I obtain the grace to receive back my lot without hindrance. For I fear your love, lest it wrong me. For it is easy for you to do what you want, but it is difficult for me to attain God, if you do not spare me.
orientation: Ignatius, bishop of Antioch, writes as a prisoner being taken to Rome, and here he begins his letter to the Roman church by expressing both his joy at the prospect of seeing them and his fear that their love might prevent his martyrdom.

title: Silence lets Ignatius become God's word
english: I do not want you to please human beings, but to please God, just as you already do. For I will never again have such an opportunity to attain God, nor will you, if you keep silent, be able to have a greater work credited to you. For if you keep silent about me, I will be a word of God; but if you love my flesh, I will be a voice again.

Grant me nothing more than to be poured out as a drink offering to God, while the altar is still ready, so that in love you may become a chorus and sing to the Father in Christ Jesus, because God has deemed the bishop of Syria worthy to be found in the west, having summoned him from the east. It is good to sink from the world toward God, so that I may rise into him.
orientation: Ignatius, bishop of Antioch, writes to the church in Rome while being taken under guard to martyrdom, urging them not to prevent his death.

title: True Christianity is not persuasion but greatness, seen when hated by the world
english: You have never envied anyone; you taught others. And I want the commands you give as disciples to be firm as well.

Only ask for power for me, both within and without, so that I may not only speak but also wish, so that I may not only be called a Christian but also be found one. For if I am found one, I can also be called one, and then I can be faithful, when I am no longer visible to the world.

Nothing visible is good. For our God Jesus Christ is seen all the more now that he is in the Father. Christianity is not a work of persuasion but of greatness, and it is shown when it is hated by the world.
orientation: Ignatius is writing to the church in Rome, urging them not to interfere with his coming martyrdom, and here he asks for prayer that he may be a real Christian, not just one in name.

title: Wheat ground by beasts into pure bread
english: I am writing to all the churches and declaring to everyone that I die willingly for God, unless you prevent me. I beg you: do not show me a kindness that comes at the wrong time. Let me be food for the beasts, for through them I can attain God. I am God's wheat, and I am ground by the teeth of the beasts, so that I may be found pure bread of Christ.

Coax the beasts instead, so that they may become my tomb and leave nothing of my body behind, so that when I have fallen asleep I may burden no one. Then I will truly be a disciple of Jesus Christ, when the world no longer sees even my body. Pray to Christ for me, so that through these instruments I may be found a sacrifice.

I do not give you orders as Peter and Paul did. They were apostles; I am a condemned man. They were free; I am still a slave. But if I suffer, I will become a freedman of Jesus Christ and will rise in him free. Now, bound as I am, I am learning to desire nothing.
orientation: Ignatius, bishop of Antioch, writes to the church in Rome while being taken under guard to martyrdom, and here he begs them not to prevent his death by wild beasts.

title: From Syria to Rome: beasts, soldiers, and the wish for Christ
english: From Syria all the way to Rome I am fighting wild beasts, through land and sea, night and day, bound to ten leopards, by which I mean a squad of soldiers. The better they are treated, the worse they become. Yet through their wrongdoings I am being made a disciple all the more, though I am not justified by this.

May I have joy of the beasts prepared for me, and I pray that they will be found prompt for me. I will even flatter them to devour me quickly, not as with some, whom they timidly refused to touch. And if they themselves are unwilling and refuse, I will force them.

Forgive me: I know what is good for me. Now I am beginning to be a disciple. May nothing of things visible and invisible envy me, so that I may attain Jesus Christ. Fire and cross and packs of beasts, cuttings, tearings, scatterings of bones, mangling of limbs, grinding of the whole body, evil punishments of the devil, let them come upon me, only so that I may attain Jesus Christ.
orientation: Ignatius, bishop of Antioch, is writing to the Roman church while being taken under guard from Syria to Rome, where he expects to be martyred by wild beasts.

title: Death is gain, not the world
english: The ends of the world and the kingdoms of this age will profit me nothing. It is better for me to die into Christ Jesus than to reign over the ends of the earth. I seek the one who died for us; I want the one who rose for us. The pangs of my birth are upon me.

Forgive me, brothers and sisters: do not hinder me from living, do not wish me to die. Do not hand over to the world the one who wants to belong to God, and do not deceive him with worldly things. Let me receive pure light; when I arrive there, I will be a human being.
Allow me to be an imitator of the passion of my God. If anyone has him within himself, let him understand what I want, and let him suffer with me, knowing what constrains me.
orientation: Ignatius, bishop of Antioch, is writing to the church in Rome while being taken under guard to martyrdom there, and he is urging them not to prevent his death.

title: The ruler of this age wants to destroy me; my love is crucified
english: The ruler of this age wants to seize me and corrupt my purpose toward God. So let none of you who are present help him. Instead, take my side, which is God's side. Do not speak the name of Jesus Christ while you long for the world.

Let no envy dwell among you. And even if I, when I am present, urge you otherwise, do not be persuaded by me. Be persuaded instead by what I am writing to you. For I write to you while I am alive, longing to die. My earthly love has been crucified, and there is no fire in me that longs for material things. But living water is speaking within me, and from inside me it says: "Come to the Father."

I take no pleasure in the food of corruption or in the pleasures of this life. I want the bread of God, which is the flesh of Jesus Christ, who is from the seed of David, and I want his blood as drink, which is incorruptible love.
orientation: Ignatius, bishop of Antioch, is writing to the Roman church while being taken under guard to Rome, where he expects to be martyred by wild beasts, and he is urging them not to prevent his death.

title: No longer living according to men
english: I no longer want to live by human standards. And this will happen if you wish it. Wish it, so that you too may be wished for.

Through these few lines I ask you: believe me. And Jesus Christ will reveal these things to you, showing that I speak truly. He is the mouth that does not lie, through which the Father has truly spoken.

Ask on my behalf, so that I may attain it. I have written to you not according to the flesh, but according to the mind of God. If I suffer, it will be because you wished it. If I am rejected, it will be because you hated me.
orientation: Ignatius is closing his letter to the Romans, telling them he no longer wants to live in a merely human way and asking them to pray that he may attain God.

title: Remember the Syrian church in prayer
english: Remember in your prayers the church in Syria, which now has God as its shepherd in my place. Jesus Christ alone will be its bishop, and your love will watch over it.

As for me, I am ashamed to be counted among them, for I am not worthy. I am the last of them and an untimely birth, as Paul said of himself. But I have been shown mercy to be someone, if I attain to God.

My spirit greets you, and so does the love of the churches that welcomed me in the name of Jesus Christ, not as one merely passing through. Even the churches that were not on my route according to the flesh escorted me ahead from city to city.
orientation: Ignatius is closing his letter to the Ephesians, asking them to pray for the church in Syria and reflecting on his own unworthiness.

title: Closing greetings and travel news from Smyrna
english: I am writing this to you from Smyrna, through the Ephesians who are worthy of blessing. Crocus is with me as well, along with many others, and his name is dear to me.

As for those who went ahead of me from Syria to Rome for the glory of God, I trust you have come to know them. Let them know that I am near. They are all worthy of God and of you, and it is fitting for you to refresh them in every way.
I wrote this to you on the ninth day before the Kalends of September. Farewell to the end, in the endurance of Jesus Christ.
orientation: Ignatius is closing his letter to the Ephesians, telling them he writes from Smyrna and asking them to care for his companions who went ahead to Rome.
